name: TimeSynchMsg
summary: Server-to-client time sync, wire 0x14f (type index 335). A 12-byte record: the 4-byte typed header (00 01 then the prefix varint 8f 05) followed by an 8-byte body. The body is a constant 2-byte prefix `0b 88` and a 48-bit big-endian counter that counts NANOSECONDS. Four captured samples advance at real time: 0.104 s, 3.038 s and 3.000 s across seqs 0x0a/0x27/0x3c/0x54, and the two long gaps each span exactly three captured pings, whose own 1 s period cross-checks the scale. The counter does NOT share an axis with PingMsg: both advance at 1 s per second but the ping sits at 122.0e12 and this message at 155.5e12, so they are two independent uptime clocks, not one session clock and not wall clock (no known epoch produces a real date).
purpose: Named by the client's own type registry as a time sync. What the client DOES with the value is not measured: the counter's base (9.3 h offset from the ping) is unresolved, so no claim is made about which clock it carries.

created_when: the capture sends it at seq 0x0a, after the registration rungs and before the level info
lifecycle.if_absent: not measured; the ladder above does not record this message as the one that moves any rung

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): the type marker 00 01 followed by the prefix varint 8f 05 = 335 = 0x14f, so the 8-byte body starts at record offset 0x04. The measured prefix varint table gives 0x14f = 8f 05, and all four committed records carry that header verbatim.

fields.name: unresolved_prefix
fields.note: Measured `0b 88` in all four committed 0x14f bodies. Constant across the four samples, so it is carried as a fixed 2-byte run rather than interpreted as an integer. It is NOT the same prefix PingMsg carries (`00 03`), so the two messages are distinguishable by their own first two body bytes as well as by wire id.
fields.provenance: PingMsg's card (flow.world-entry.rung.ping) carries the same measured shape with a different constant: `00 03` then the 48-bit counter

fields.name: time_high
fields.note: Top 16 bits of the 48-bit counter. Read with time_low as ONE 48-bit big-endian nanosecond counter, the same split PingMsg uses because the closed codec vocabulary has no 48-bit integer. Measured 8d68 in seq 0x0a/0x27 and 8d69 in seq 0x3c/0x54, and the step between those two halves is what the 3 s gaps predict.
fields.provenance: meanings.md 'The first typed exchange, measured' (seq 0x0a R 0x14f 12 bytes TimeSynchMsg); the 48-bit split follows the measured 0x15d tick

fields.name: time_low
fields.note: Low 32 bits of the same counter. The four samples are 0x7b13001a, 0x8141abb4, 0x365cc1e0, 0xe92f11ff and their gaps are 103721882 ns, 3038451244 ns and 3000127519 ns - i.e 0.104 s, 3.038 s, 3.000 s. The two long gaps each span exactly three captured PingMsg records, whose measured period is 1.000 s (nine consecutive gaps between 1.0005 and 1.0019 s), so two independent series agree on the scale.
fields.provenance: capture: the four 0x14f_R records and the ten 0x15d_R pings in services/world/replay/messages-redacted.txt

evidence.ref: services/world/replay/messages-redacted.txt: four R-direction 0x14f records at seq 0x0a, 0x27, 0x3c, 0x54, each 12 bytes = 00 01 8f 05 + 8-byte body, no redaction. Parsed by a full-corpus byte pass (177 records read, 138 of them R)

scale cross-check: the ten R-direction 0x15d pings in the same dump have nine consecutive gaps of 1001566199/1000565000/1000566800/1001453500/1000488800/1001303701/1000446800/1000554799/1001862801 ns, and the 0x27->0x3c and 0x3c->0x54 0x14f gaps (3038451244 and 3000127519 ns) span exactly three pings each
research/atlas/meanings.md 'The first typed exchange, measured': seq 0x0a is R 0x14f 12 bytes 'TimeSynchMsg'. The name is the client's own; the type table index is 335

the two counters do not share an axis: PingMsg spans 122005786537332..122014795345732 ns over the capture while 0x14f spans 155479880957978..155486023258623 ns at the same sequence positions, a 9.3 h offset, and neither offset resolves to a real date under the 1970, 2001 or 1601 epochs. Recorded as measured and NOT interpreted
